key_insight: In a small randomized placebo-controlled phase I trial, an oral polypore fungi combination (FoTv) appeared safe and was associated with fewer COVID-19 symptoms and lower inflammatory markers.
clinical_relevance: This early study suggests a low-cost, at-home supportive option may be feasible for non-hospitalized mild-to-moderate COVID-19, but it is not enough to establish treatment efficacy.
method: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I trial
26 participants received FoTv and 24 received placebo at two medical centers
Safety labs, symptom burden, adherence, and exploratory antiviral/inflammatory signals were assessed
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high adherence, low dropout, normal-range safety labs overall, and exploratory improvements in symptoms and C-reactive protein, plus reduced pseudovirus infection in vitro.
watch_item: This is a small phase I study with exploratory endpoints, so the findings need confirmation in larger trials before any clinical use claims.
paper_title: Safety, Feasibility, and Preliminary Clinical Findings of an Oral Polypore Fungi Combination with Mild-to-Moderate COVID-19: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase I Clinical Trial
